Integrate information security continuity planning with the organization’s overall risk management and business continuity strategies.
Establish a process for continuous improvement based on lessons learned from drills, adverse events, or changes in business context.

control_results.control_name: Compliance with Legal and Contractual Requirements
control_results.score_rationale: The policy demonstrates formal documentation of compliance with legal and contractual requirements, assigns accountability, and outlines regular risk assessment and monitoring, but lacks explicit procedures for ongoing identification, documentation, and updating of all relevant requirements and does not detail a process for maintaining an up-to-date compliance inventory.
evidence: It is the policy of Provider to comply, and to require its employees to comply, with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations, as well as Provider’s policies and procedures, governing information security, confidentiality, and privacy.
Provider established an Information Security Program (the “Program”) to assure compliance with applicable laws.
The Coordinator will be responsible for ensuring that company staff is trained in the relevant legal requirements for handling and storing Information.
Provider will designate an Information Security Program Coordinator (“Coordinator”) who will be primarily responsible for coordinating and overseeing the Program.

Provider will take steps to identify and assess internal and external risks to the security, confidentiality, and integrity of Information that could result in the unauthorized access, disclosure, misuse, alteration, destruction or other compromise of such Information.
gaps: No explicit process for identifying all relevant legislative, regulatory, and contractual requirements.
Absence of a documented mechanism for keeping legal and contractual requirements up to date.
Does not address regular review or update of compliance requirements inventory.
recommendations: Establish a formal procedure for identifying and documenting all relevant legislative, regulatory, and contractual requirements.
Implement a process for regularly reviewing and updating the inventory of compliance obligations.
Assign responsibility and accountability for maintaining current documentation of legal and contractual requirements.
Integrate compliance requirement updates into risk assessments and business process reviews.

control_results.score_rationale: The policy establishes a formal, documented process for periodic reviews of the information security program and references independent evaluation by a designated Coordinator, but does not explicitly require independent (third-party or internal independent) reviews as specified in the requirement.
evidence: This Program will be reviewed and adjusted periodically. The Coordinator will review the Program annually to ensure ongoing compliance, as well as consistency with other existing and future laws and regulations.
The Coordinator will provide periodic reports on the status of the Program and note any changes to the overall risk assessment and changes to established safeguards.

Some areas of the company may require more frequent review than others, such as IT, records management, or any other area that comes in contact with a high volume of Information or is especially vulnerable to technological or procedural risks and threats.
The Coordinator will establish procedures for identifying and assessing risks in each relevant area of Provider’s operations outlined above.
gaps: No explicit requirement that reviews of the information security program or its implementation are conducted independently (by an internal party not responsible for day-to-day security or by an external auditor).
No mention of third-party assessments or internal audit department involvement.
No details on the scope, methodology, evidence retention, or reporting to senior management for security reviews.
recommendations: Explicitly require that information security reviews are performed by independent parties, such as an internal audit function separate from the security team or qualified external auditors.
Document the scope and methodology of the security reviews and record evidence of assessment findings.
Include a requirement to report the findings of independent reviews to senior management or the board, along with remediation plans.
Monitor results of these reviews and incorporate lessons learned to continuously improve the security program.
